core_obligations: Show the Gysin map exists by exhibiting X -> X x_k Y as an immersion into a smooth scheme over Y (proof lines 14443-14448).
Reduce to the smooth equidimensional case and express alpha, beta through caps of bivariant classes (proof lines 14450-14462).
Move f^! through the product using commutation with bivariant classes and the value on the fundamental class (proof lines 14464-14476).
proof_roadmap: Existence and reduction to equidimensional components (proof lines 14443-14452).
Representation of the classes as caps (proof lines 14454-14462).
difficulty_reason: For a field k and a morphism f : X -> Y of schemes smooth over k, the lemma asserts that the Gysin map exists for f and that f^!(alpha . beta) = f^!alpha . f^!beta (statement lines 14436-14441). The proof first notes that X -> X x_k Y is an immersion of X into a scheme smooth over Y, so the Gysin map exists by Definition labelled definition-lci-gysin, then reduces to the case where X and Y are smooth and equidimensional of dimensions d and e by decomposing into connected components (proof lines 14443-14452). With f^![Y]_e = [X]_d from Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy and the identifications alpha = c cap [Y]_e, beta = c' cap [Y]_e given by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, the proof notes that alpha . beta = c cap c' cap [Y]_e and that f^! commutes with c and c' by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, then runs a six term chain of equalities moving f^! onto the fundamental class and back (proof lines 14454-14476). An alternative proof via (f x f)^!(alpha x beta) = f^!alpha x f^!beta and Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-composition is also recorded (proof lines 14478-14479). Representing Chow classes of smooth schemes as caps of bivariant classes and using commutation of f^! with them is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
